literal: Even in the presence of the mother who bore one, it is unpleasant; what then of intoxication in the presence of the noble?
translation: Drunkenness is painful even in the presence of one's own mother. How much worse will it be before the wise?
modern: பெற்ற தாயின் முன்னிலையிலும் குடிப்பழக்கம் துன்பம் தருவதாகும்; அப்படியிருக்க, சான்றோர்களின் முன்னிலையில் குடித்து மயங்குவது பற்றி என்ன சொல்வது?
explanation: This couplet highlights the universal disgrace of drunkenness. A mother's love is naturally forgiving and unconditional, yet even she finds her child's intoxication painful and repulsive. The poet uses this extreme example to ask a rhetorical question: if even a mother cannot bear the sight of drunkenness, how much more offensive will it be to the wise and noble, who judge by virtue and reason? The word 'களி' (intoxication) is contrasted with the presence of 'சான்றோர்' (the noble) to emphasize the incompatibility of vice and virtue.
